ios.desc:
Take the long way home.

Need a quick walk? Point the compass at the nearest konbini or coffee spot. Have a little more time? Mix up a suggested detour, stop at a café and a quiet shrine, or add a pitstop on the way to a station.

FOLLOW. WALK. STAMP.
Choose a destination, follow the bearing and press a tactile Riso-style illustrated stamp when you arrive. The compass gives direction, not turn-by-turn navigation. Distance and time estimates are approximate; choose a safe, public way there.

YOUR POCKET STAMP BOOK
Keep recorded days in Logroll, replay a day's Journey and export a recap. Field Guide starts with Your Footprint: the neighbourhoods and prefectures you have visited. Save a favourite spot for another day.

EVERYDAY PLACES STAY FREE
Konbini, supermarkets, nearby Tokyo-area stations and saved places stay free. Your first five standalone curated stamps are free, plus three curated detours with a separate local allowance. A detour uses one allowance at its first successful curated stamp; all original stops stay included after restarting, without using standalone stamps. Browsing, shuffling, starting and cancelling before that stamp are free. Successful new standalone curated stamps use the stamp allowance; repeats and failed saves do not. Collected stamps stay in your book.

GO FURTHER WITH ACHIRA PRO
Explore unlimited curated cafés, shrines, sento, independent shops and sights, and curated detours. Pro includes chain filters, nearby nudges and Apple Watch support on iOS. See current prices and any trial in the app.

MADE FOR WALKING, EVEN OFFLINE
The place catalogue travels with you. No account, sign-in or ads. Saved Home and Hotel coordinates stay on your device. Validation analytics exclude raw GPS and saved labels, and follow your analytics settings.

One more corner. One more stamp. A little more Japan in your book.

Privacy: https://nicebits.jp/apps/privacy
Terms: https://nicebits.jp/apps/tos

quotes.text:
I made a simple wee Konbini compass* app for whenever I'm ambling around Tokyo so I no longer have to go through the (_so heavy_) process of opening a map app, changing to jp keyboard and typing `konbini` to reliably find something.

Instead it's just a compass face, with brand and distance.

It's free for basic konbini hunting (has probably most of the stored in Japan), and is offline first. So maybe it's useful to other folk?? (I hope so!)

There's some stamp-book style collection things in there too, but that's more fun, and a few `PRO` gated things (more stats, filtering... soon some other store types). But none of it required for finding the next Biru or coffee.

*https://apps.apple.com/us/app/achira-japan-offline-guide/id6768049512
